subject: BCOG
title: Introduction to Programming for the Brain and Cognitive Sciences

restrictions: Restricted to Brain and Cognitive Science major(s).
Restricted to students in the Psychology department.
sections.sectionText: By the end of the course, students will have developed a piece of software of their choice (e.g., a simple experiment, video game, etc.). Core topics include program design, data wrangling and visualization, reproducible workflows (version control, environments), experiment/game scripting, statistical modeling, and simple machine-learning pipelines. Prior coding experience not required; familiarity with quantitative research methods recommended. RESTRICTED CLASS: Restricted to BCOG majors until Thursday, Nov. 19 at approx. 9:00 A.M.

subject: BCOG
title: Capstone Undergraduate Research
info: 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated in separate semesters for a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours. The fall offering of the course will focus on identifying a research question and writing a comprehensive review of the literature bearing on the research question. The spring offering of the course will focus on writing the empirical results of the experiment/study and writing a discussion of the results, placing the study findings in the context of the literature. Prerequisite: Senior standing in Brain and Cognitive Sciences, and consent of instructor. Students must arrange to do a research project with a faculty member. Restricted to Brain & Cognitive Science majors.
